fig1_model.caption: Model rules and one recorded encounter. (a) Both dolphin target policies use the same 2T near-prey herding cycle, one feasible strike and normal handling/recovery. Gannets influence dolphins through prey dynamics, without a dolphin response to a bird cue. (b,c) Actual top and side views at 12T for development school 39061002, exposed targeting with gannets; lines show predator paths over 6–12T and crosses mark actual captures in that interval. Horizontal coordinates are relative to the surviving fish centroid at 12T; z=0 is the surface. Coordinates are model units. This snapshot illustrates the model, not successful whole-school containment.

fig2_development.caption: Development comparison of the two dolphin target-selection rules. Bars show actual dolphin captures in matched 36T encounters with 12 dolphins, with or without 3 gannets. Each policy was tested on the same two development schools with one random-stream setting. Nearest targeting changed from 55 to 53 captures in total; exposed targeting changed from 41 to 48. The exposed policy was selected for follow-up on this development evidence. Individual school outcomes are shown without confidence intervals.

fig4_mechanism.caption: Matching gannet-only controls and initial-depth results. (a) Dolphin capture change (DG minus D) and gannet change (DG minus G) for the same four fresh-school comparisons. S1=39063501 and S2=39063502; repetitions 1 and 2 identify settings 61001 and 61002. Both species improve in two repetitions; four comparisons represent two independent schools. (b) Gannet-only captures over 36T across initial vertical translations, using setting 61001; lines join the same school, not fitted response curves. (c) Fraction of surviving fish within the reference target-depth envelope 7.93028, with colour identifying initial mean depth and solid/dashed lines identifying schools 1/2. This is a geometric eligibility reference, not guaranteed interception. Initial depth is not maintained; movement and selective removal can alter the survivor fraction. No uncertainty intervals are shown.

fig3_replication.caption: Fresh-school replication of the frozen exposed-target policy. (a) Actual dolphin captures with and without gannets for two fresh schools crossed with two random-stream settings; labels 61001 and 61002 identify those settings. (b) The within-pair capture difference; S1 and S2 denote schools 39063501 and 39063502. All encounters last 36T and retain identical dolphin rules and starting conditions within each pair. Four stochastic comparisons represent two independent school configurations, not four independent schools. No confidence intervals are shown.
